answer: Continuous physical-presence beacon. Each operator runs a hardware device that samples its own sensor plume—ambient light, vibration, radio noise—and signs a rolling hash every few seconds. Agents transacting must embed the latest signed sample. A verifier compares samples against the live ridge of co-located devices, rejecting identities whose samples never diverge. Faking requires operating N distinct physical sites with genuine sensor variation, so a farm of clones collapses to one signature. The lantern metric: per-identity cost = one maintained physical location plus power and hardware,
